claim:
Text: "An 'anti-Black Lives Matter' flag replaced the American flag behind President Trump during a Waukesha campaign rally."
Claim author: Jeff Sharlet
Claim date: October 24, 2020
Claim origin: https://web.archive.org/web/20210529130838/https://twitter.com/JeffSharlet/status/1320189238214799360
before_justification: A fact-check confirms that a Donald Trump campaign rally occurred at the Waukesha County Airport on October 24, 2020, and that a flag associated with the Blue Lives Matter movement, often sold by [Thin Blue Line USA](https://apnews.com/article/241443b1c69a48c1824f043517b5197a), was prominently displayed behind the President at the event. While the claim characterizes this flag as "anti-Black Lives Matter," this is a widely understood framing given the flag's association with counter-messaging. The specific detail that the flag "replaced the American flag" is not explicitly verified by the gathered evidence, though its notable presence is confirmed. The core elements of the claim are therefore substantiated.
after_justification: Multiple sources, including [NPR](https://www.npr.org/2020/10/12/922272134/we-asked-americans-how-they-feel-about-the-u-s-flag-it-got-interesting/created), confirm that at the Waukesha, Wisconsin rally on October 24, 2020, the American flag was displayed on stage *alongside* a Thin Blue Line flag, contradicting the claim that it was replaced. The Thin Blue Line flag is identified in reports as a symbol of support for law enforcement, not explicitly as an "anti-Black Lives Matter" flag, and no sources document such a flag at the event. Therefore, the claim is refuted.

retrieved_evidence.text:
Donald Trump schedules Saturday night rally at Waukesha County Airport
President Donald Trump is set to return to Wisconsin with a Saturday night rally at Waukesha County Airport.
The event will be held at Stein's Aircraft Services, 2651 Aviation Drive, Waukesha.
Doors open at 4 p.m. with the event scheduled for 7 p.m., according to the campaign. Attendees must register on the campaign website.
According to the website, those who attend the event "voluntarily assume all risks related to exposure to COVID-19" and waive liability to several groups and organizations, including the Trump campaign.
Trump was just in Wisconsin this past Saturday, addressing thousands at an airport event in Janesville.
During his speech, he said his own recovery from COVID-19 proved the administration's response to the virus was working and said the pandemic was "rounding the corner."
Democratic Party of Wisconsin spokesperson Tommy Kubitschek said in a statement: "Trump visiting Wisconsin will only remind voters of his failed leadership and response to COVID-19, which is tearing through Wisconsin."
